title: Tor amplitude of exact sections on the geometric point
statement: Let F be the finite-field datum of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], k its algebraically closed field, and A a finite commutative ring. Let K be any object of the recorded pro-etale derived category of A-modules on Spec(k) [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. If K has intrinsic pro-etale Tor amplitude in [a,b] [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], then the derived final-object sections, with coefficient ring ULift A and the canonical constant-section scalar map [def-weil-point-section-scalar-functors], have ordinary module Tor amplitude in [a,b]. No constructibility or finite-generation hypothesis on K or on the tensor test modules is imposed.

proof.text: Transport the Tor predicate to the fixed-scalar module-sheaf category through the exact intrinsic realization equivalence, using [lem-exc-intrinsic-tor-amplitude-transport] and [def-sp-finite-coefficient-intrinsic-derived-comparison]. The bounded flat-model theorem [lem-trf-source-bounded-flat-tor-amplitude] gives a flat-term representative supported in [a,b].

source.place: Step 1: geometric-point passage, finite free models, and reversed-degree duals

proof.text: After intrinsic realization, restriction along the constant-scalar map recovers each original sheaf term via the sheafification counit and fully faithful realization. This is the concrete encoding of [def-pur-proetale-module-scalar-restriction]. At the identity geometric point, the pointed final neighbourhood is initial (the structured arrow of the identity). Its opposite is terminal, so its colimit injection is an isomorphism. Use the geometric-point/stalk comparison constructed in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-finite-model-stalks] to identify this final-object evaluation with the sheaf fibre. The proved source-library Point.flat_sheafFiber_obj preserves flatness. Therefore each section term is flat. The scalar action agrees by the concrete definitions of restriction and [def-weil-point-section-scalar-functors].

source.place: Step 1: geometric-point passage, finite free models, and reversed-degree duals

proof.text: The additive sections functor sends the zero terms outside [a,b] to zero. Its exact derived localization comparison identifies this section complex with derived sections of K. Apply [lem-trf-source-bounded-flat-tor-amplitude] to this bounded flat complex and transfer the Tor predicate along that comparison.

theorem point_sections_torAmplitude (F : FiniteFieldDatum.{u})
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Finite A] (K : proEtaleDerivedCategory (Spec (.of F.k)) A)
    (a b : ℤ) (hTor : HasProEtaleTorAmplitude (Spec (.of F.k)) A K a b) :
    DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1, u} A)) a b
      ((pointFiniteSections F.k A).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)
